metadata.summary: CheXpert is a large chest radiograph dataset containing 224,316 chest radiographs of 65,240 patients. It includes automatically extracted labels for 14 observations from radiology reports, with explicit uncertainty annotations to reflect interpretation variability.
metadata.purpose: To serve as a standard benchmark for training and evaluating deep learning models on chest radiograph interpretation, particularly addressing uncertainty in radiological reporting.

papers.title: CheXpert — A Large Chest Radiograph Dataset with Uncertainty Labels and Expert Comparison

ethics.privacy_measures: De-identification performed per HIPAA Safe Harbor standards; all protected health information (PHI) removed or generalized.
ethics.legal_compliance: Compliant with HIPAA and Stanford IRB Protocol #35571.

extraction.notes: Baseline card derived solely from dataset_catalog.xlsx real metadata; remaining fields require paper/README or manual completion.
pending_verification: geography.countries is heuristically inferred from limitation text; requires manual verification

known_limitations: Single-center origin limits generalizability to other institutions, imaging protocols, or patient demographics.
Labels are report-derived, not ground-truth clinical diagnoses; may reflect reporting bias or documentation practices rather than true disease status.
No demographic metadata (age, sex, race/ethnicity) released with the dataset.
Frontal/lateral views only; no CT or other modalities included.
bias_and_limitations.modifications: Yes — labels were algorithmically generated from radiology reports using custom NLP rules; uncertainty semantics were added post-hoc.
bias_and_limitations.representativeness_concerns: Highly limited to Stanford Hospital population; no demographic or geographic diversity reported.
bias_and_limitations.long_tail_classes: Some observations (e.g., 'Enlarged Cardiomediastinum', 'Pleural Other') are rare and exhibit class imbalance.
bias_and_limitations.generalizability_statement: Performance may degrade on images from different manufacturers, acquisition protocols, or non-academic settings due to domain shift.
bias_and_limitations.missing_data: Demographic attributes (age, sex, ethnicity) are not included in the public release; label blanks represent missing report mentions, not verified absences.

data_origin.selection_rationale: Radiographs were selected from the electronic health record (EHR) system at Stanford Hospital; inclusion was based on availability of frontal and lateral chest radiographs with associated radiology reports.

population.target_population: Adult patients undergoing chest radiography at Stanford Hospital
population.inclusion_criteria: Frontal and lateral chest radiographs with associated radiology reports in Stanford’s EHR.

attribute_recording.unknown_proportion: Uncertainty labels (e.g., 'uncertain', 'negative', 'positive', 'blank') reflect ambiguity in report text; blank entries indicate absence of mention, not confirmed absence.
attribute_recording.recoding_modifications: Labels were automatically extracted and mapped to 14 observation categories using rule-based NLP; uncertainty semantics were encoded per label.

annotation.annotation_method: Rule-based NLP labeler applied to radiology reports to extract presence/absence/uncertainty for 14 observations.
annotation.labeling_provenance: Labels derived from free-text radiology reports via automated extraction; validated against expert annotations on subsets.
annotation.label_noise_description: Label noise arises from ambiguity in report language (e.g., 'no evidence of pneumonia' vs. 'pneumonia ruled out'), inconsistent phrasing, and missing mentions (blanks). Uncertainty labels explicitly capture this.
